note: The local test package is not release-certified. Statuses: pass (the aspect's stated scope is evidenced and passes; what the criterion needs beyond that scope is its own not-run aspect), fail (an observed or recorded correctness failure), blocked (cannot be exercised because of a recorded failure or an unsupported capability), not-run (no evidence yet). A criterion is fail if any aspect fails, otherwise blocked if any is blocked, otherwise not-run if any has not run, otherwise pass. An aspect is graded when the criterion's text or the one-shot scenario it names asks for it; play the criterion does not name and that no run exercised is listed under the criterion's notExercised, ungraded. Deferred certification is listed once, under deferredCertification, and is not part of any criterion's status. Built by tools/build_acceptance_index.py; MMR-1 adds the final scenario.

criteria.text: A pinned FWGC++ build and version-matched Bannerlord/Modding Kit/War Sails setup are reproducibly identified and verified; the existing stale generator binary is not accepted as installation evidence.

aspects.aspect: the producer is pinned and its build verified
aspects.note: fwg.exe 564c2629... from FWGC++ commit ec5d1c10; CTest 5/5; MMR-22 22/22 lock and process checks. tests/check_producer_lock.py re-checks the lock, the binary and the FWGC++ checkout. Whether a fresh build reproduces the pinned bytes is not shown; tools/Build-Fwg.ps1 does not check out the pinned commit.

aspects.aspect: the stale generator binary is not accepted
aspects.note: Any binary other than the pin is refused before launch (pin_mismatch), by the deploy, the package and the module itself. The stale binary in the FWGC++ tree (generator/build/apps/Release/fwg.exe) hashes 5867006c40876b4c..., not the pin (hashed by this audit, 2026-10-18).

aspects.aspect: the game and War Sails versions are identified and pinned
aspects.note: Bannerlord v1.4.8.119303 and War Sails v1.2.8.119303; 25 assemblies (18 game, 6 framework, Harmony) and 6 descriptors pinned by SHA-256; build and deploy refuse other inputs. The final one-shot run recorded the same versions and the package's module, fwg.exe and worldbridge.exe hashes.

aspects.aspect: the Modding Kit is identified
aspects.note: Identified by its Steam depot 4456490 and manifest 1015157637537524692 and one editor session that opened and rendered the War Sails map (2026-10-13; the record is an inspection, so it says ticketAccepted false). No build or player step uses it. Not re-checked since.

aspects.aspect: generation is reproducible
aspects.note: MMR-24 75/75 identity and retry checks; MMR-23 120/120 source contract checks (re-run 2026-10-19). The shipped worldbridge (2bfdbb9d...) republished all 19 accepted bundles of the 2026-10-19 seed sweep byte for byte (seed-yield.json reproduced), worlds A and B with their content ids f596b58c... and f63c6841... unchanged.

aspects.aspect: the producer's pinned runtime matches this installation
aspects.note: A Windows update (KB5127647/KB5127648, 2026-10-13/14) replaced C:\Windows\System32\ucrtbase.dll after the pin; the UCRT pin in worldgen/producer.lock.json was renewed to the installed dedb7611... on 2026-10-19 (fix the failures: the owner's instruction). The producer process contract's preflight passes again (Test-ProducerProcess in the offline suites). The producer lock is not a world input inside the bundle, so no world content id changed.

criteria.text: Bannerlord's New Campaign flow generates a fresh chosen-seed world locally with progress/cancel/error handling, without a player running an external editor, publishing a module or restarting the game.

aspects.aspect: New Procedural Campaign entry and setup screen
aspects.note: MMR-43 run 13032 19/19; 29 offline checks.

aspects.aspect: the generation job: progress, cancel and errors, in the running game
aspects.note: MMR-44 run 21316 17/17: cancel in 4 phases, a killed producer gives generate.crashed, largest frame gap 0.407 s. The final one-shot run cancelled a generation through the setup screen (step 6) and recorded seed 43's refusal with its code and action. No external editor, module publishing or restart.

aspects.aspect: preview, regeneration and Start Campaign
aspects.note: MMR-46 run 50304 16/16; MMR-45 run 43676 15/15. The final one-shot run (step 1, run 40412) generated A from the New Campaign screen in 35.7 s, finished character creation and entered the map after 395.3 s; its preview matched the live campaign (run 50244).

aspects.aspect: an interrupted generation is recovered
aspects.note: MMR-47 crash run 28280 and resume run 47264, 8/8.

aspects.aspect: the measured first-test profile
aspects.note: MMR-56 run 35468 20/20, re-measured by the final one-shot run 40412. The first Start Campaign blocks the engine thread about 6.5 minutes while the navigation caches are built (the game does not respond); the wait text says so.

aspects.aspect: the clean package generates and starts a world
aspects.note: The final package e20f2667... installed alone generated and started world A (one-shot step 1) and passed the clean-install sequence (s7).

aspects.aspect: a chosen seed gives a playable world
aspects.note: Owner's judgement asked: chosen seeds now generally give a playable world, not every one. Offline, seeds 42-73 at one quality attempt went from 1 of 32 accepted to 19 of 32 (town repairs, port and village repairs, binding), and all 19 pass every managed activation stage offline: settlements, the runtime navigation build and validator over the stand-in engine, and the naval, spawn, graph, faction, character, registry and water stages (seed-yield.json). A request gets 3 quality attempts with derived seeds. In game, seeds 42 (A) and 73 (B) were played through the final one-shot run; seed 43 generated its third attempt's world, which the in-game navigation validator refused (runtime.navigation_refused: one sea route across the seam 1.29 x the mesh's shortest path, against 1.25), with its error code and a Generate-again action. The stand-in engine cannot see that detour; a runtime refusal ends the job instead of trying the next derived seed (follow-up).

criteria.text: The entire generated globe is playable as a flat map with connected east/west edges. Terrain, player/AI land and naval routes, distances, encounters, camera/picking and saves use one consistent periodic topology; different seeds change geography and traversability.

aspects.aspect: periodic coordinates and distances
aspects.note: MMR-64 run 6292 16/16; 85 offline checks on world A (re-run 2026-10-19 with the enlarged spatial table). East-west distances overstate sphere distance by 1/cos(latitude) (docs/periodic-coordinates.md).

aspects.aspect: generated terrain renders and answers heights, rays and picking
aspects.note: MMR-16 run 32896; MMR-37 32/32. Exact native bin-boundary rounding is unresolved (docs/runtime-backend-decision.md R02).

aspects.aspect: land and naval routes agree with the engine on generated worlds
aspects.note: MMR-38 run 42984: world A 826/826 routes, world B 1118/1118; MMR-41 21/21 with navigation caches cold, reused and faulted. The final one-shot run activated A and B on the shipped bridge (both navigation reports activatable).

aspects.aspect: travel, camera and picking across the seam
aspects.note: On world A the final one-shot run (two_world_matrix create 43576) crossed the seam on land, was pursued across it, called a fleet across it and kept it all through save and load. On world B (seam_presentation 44028, MMR-66's sections on a generated world): display copies, camera follow and pan, fast moves, picking (copy rays equal canonical rays), tracks, alignment, a town menu across the seam and the wrap budget, between two towns joined by land across the seam.

aspects.aspect: different seeds change geography and traversability
aspects.note: Worlds A (seed 42) and B (seed 73) differ in every geography hash (land cells 2389 vs 4192, coastlines differ) and in their engine routes (826 vs 1118), and both are played in the final one-shot run (land missions on B included).

aspects.aspect: encounters and missions at the seam
aspects.note: The final one-shot naval run 39772: route.seam (sailed across the seam, one rebase, on naval navigation, at sea) and pirate.seam (a naval encounter of the party and a pirate 1.5 apart across the seam, its mission, the retreat). One land mission at the seam ran (MMR-42 run 17596).

aspects.aspect: one consistent topology for the audited consumers; named presentation limits
aspects.note: Owner's judgement asked: the topology is one for every audited consumer, with three named presentation limits left. Every planar campaign measure the audit found (evidence/world/periodic-consumers.tsv: 105 methods, 168 calls) is transpiled periodic, now with the views the player reads as distances (the clan screen's distance sorts, the army overlay, the game-menu party list, the nearby culture's music); the storm tick at the seam (L14) was fixed by MMR-65; strip lake copies cut by the terrain's edge now follow their twin. Left, presentation only: the hero behaviour text measures planar near the cut (its class initializer cannot run when the set is applied); siege machines and missiles are drawn only on the settlement's own side of the cut; a route whose path leaves the terrain cannot be represented (docs/periodic-presentation.md, Limits).

notExercised: mouse dragging across the seam (it pivots on the rebased click position; axis input was injected)
encyclopedia, clan and kingdom screen map navigation (FastMoveCameraToPosition called directly)
a siege, a raid, embarking and disembarking at the seam

criteria.text: Generated towns, villages, castles, factions, clans and characters initialize a coherent Sandbox campaign with trading, recruitment, ownership, wars and missions, with no unintended Calradia campaign objects surviving.

aspects.aspect: generated factions, clans, heroes, settlements and economy register and validate

recorded.status: c1-c3 evidenced for new-game initialization plus two campaign days per world; save/load, UI-driven interactions, settlement visuals and long-run economy unproved

aspects.note: World A: 358 settlements, 40 kingdoms, 92 clans. The MMR-30/33/34/35/36 in-game probes ran on 4-settlement fixtures; the whole world is covered by MMR-45, MMR-51 and the final one-shot run. One town starts with no gold and earns it within the day; 22 of 40 kingdoms hold a single fief.

aspects.aspect: no unintended Calradia campaign objects survive
aspects.note: The graph validator refuses official objects, references and coordinates; MMR-51 run 41920 found 0 settlements, clans or kingdoms outside the world.

aspects.aspect: trading, recruitment, ownership and wars
aspects.note: MMR-51 run 41920 55/55, 14 scenarios, 1 day 6 h on world A; the final one-shot run's soak (20424) travelled, traded and recruited in a generated town. Trade and recruitment drive the screens' logic without the screens. Long play is deferred certification.

aspects.aspect: land missions and mission transitions
aspects.note: The final one-shot land run 18492: 163/163 checks, 14/14 cases (field battles of every class A has and B's wetland, town, castle, village, siege, capture, hideout, crossing, retreat), each return with the world identity unchanged; MMR-60 11/11; MMR-42 11/11.

aspects.aspect: every generated world initializes
aspects.note: Worlds A and B activate and play in the final one-shot run. Offline, every one of the 19 accepted worlds of seeds 42-73 passes the activation's managed stages (seed-yield.json); the sweep found and fixed the refusals of other worlds: harbours on closed basins, unplaceable villages (a crash in three runtime readers), a deck shared by two joins and port pairs the engine cannot route.

notExercised: village raids on land, lord's hall fights, port visits
a field battle fought to the end (all ended by retreat or the probe's kills), the hideout's night stealth mission
siege preparation beyond 1.5 h; captivity escape played rather than applied

criteria.text: War Sails ports, fleets, embarkation, land/sea routes, navigation types and required distance caches operate on the generated world; naval travel and naval encounters are tested.

aspects.aspect: ports, fleets and naval faction records
aspects.note: MMR-35: 15 offline checks; in-game run 21180 on the fixture world; the final one-shot run sailed from and docked at generated ports on world A.

aspects.aspect: water, flow and weather on the generated world
aspects.note: MMR-59 23/23; MMR-39 runs on fixtures. Rivers have no water surface; 15 of 23 lake groups on world A have no plane (too shallow at the sample grid).

aspects.aspect: naval travel, embarkation and encounters

aspects.aspect: fleets survive save and load

notExercised: boarding, crew reinforcement, ship damage in battle, a naval battle won by fighting, a blockade battle or an AI blockade
straits narrower than 8.5; pirate-initiated encounters (the player was ignored); port visits

criteria.text: Two campaigns with different world identities can be saved, alternately loaded after a cold restart, and resumed with correct terrain, objects and navigation; missing or mismatched worlds fail safely before simulation.

aspects.note: The final one-shot matrix: create 43576 38/38 (A played into mutable land and naval state across the seam and saved; B, seed 73, generated, started, changed and saved; A then B loaded in the same process), cold 44704 20/20 (a new process loads A, its scene swept and re-encoded, then B; each equal to its save). deferredCertification.note: Seeds 42-73 offline at one quality attempt: 19 of 32 accepted, all 19 offline-activatable (stand-in engine). In game: 42 and 73 played, 43 refused at runtime navigation. Size 129 only; the in-game activation of the other 17 accepted seeds is not run.
The sweep runs the activation's managed stages and the stand-in navigation offline; no sweep of generated worlds through the game exists.
The longest play is 1 day 6 h on world A (MMR-51). Long-run economy, raids, sieges and naval attrition over many days are untested.
One working-set measurement per phase in one profile run.
The weather model was checked against its formula for all four seasons on fixtures; no season-long play.
One machine (Core Ultra 9, RTX 5080, 32 GB) at a 60 fps cap; narrow screens and UI scales measured, not run; no mission frame rate.
The budget is provisional and not enforced. The first start of every world, and the first start or load after a module update, blocks the engine thread for about 6.5 minutes.
